text:
sarah: :rotating_light: alert from infra metrics — GPU pool 'eu-west-3' reached 100% utilization after canary of model v13. Queue length spike, many requests in 'queued' state. Seeing KV-cache mem growth for v13.
incident-bot: INCIDENT AUTO-PAGE: gpu-pool-exhaustion (severity P1). Pager rota: oncall-night. Links: https://monitoring.example/alerts/2340156789
oncall-night: on it, grabbing logs and looking at autoscaler. Can you post the rollout ID?
sarah: rollout id: rollout-2026-03-14-v13-ctx. Manual deploy window at 01:20 UTC.
mike: quick check — metrics show 3x increase in average context length for requests to v13 vs v12, KV miss rate higher during first 10k tokens, so warmup causing KV spill and more GPU memory per session.
eli: autoscaler logs: "scaleUp blocked: maxPoolsReached for project redwood-prod-eu (limit 5)" — looks like we hit tenant/global pool limit.
sarah: confirmed. We were at 5 pools and autoscaler attempted to create pool-6 but hit quota.
oncall-night: impact? percent errors/latency?
mike: 500 error rate up from 0.1% to 2.8% for generation endpoints using v13, p95 latency from 220ms -> 2.1s. Some customers on Dedicated pools unaffected, hosted API customers impacted.
product-ops: cs reported 2 customers with errors, one on free tier with high regen traffic. Could be user-facing.
cs-rep: getting customer pings — stating completions timeout and partial responses.
oncall-night: immediate mitigation plan: 1) pause v13 rollout (stop canary flag). 2) reroute incoming traffic for v13 to v12 fallback for 10m. 3) evict heavy KV caches where safe. 4) request quota bump from infra provider or scale down other low-util pools. Who can flip the rollout?
sarah: I can flip the canary to 0% now. Doing: `/rollout abort rollout-2026-03-14-v13-ctx`
deploy-bot: Rollout abort initiated by sarah at 01:27 UTC — canary traffic set to 0%.
oncall-night: great. Step 2 reroute — do we have traffic-routing rule?
mike: setting emergency route: `curl -X POST https://internal-router/services/route -d '{"model":"v13","fallback":"v12","duration":"600s"}'` (applied).
oncall-night: step3 — KV eviction. We can run a targeted eviction on the v13 shards to free GPU mem: `cachectl evict --model v13 --shards=all --grace=30s` — this will drop warmup caches and increase initial latency but free mem. Anyone object?
eli: do it. It's safe; warmup will repopulate but that's acceptable.
sarah: running eviction now. Output: ```evict started shard 0..7; expected reclaimed 420GB total; started at 01:31 UTC```
mike: autoscaler still blocked until quota resolution. We can temporarily move some low-traffic pools in eu-west-3 to eu-central-1 and free a slot. I'll start a graceful drain of pool-2.
oncall-night: coordinate. Use drain and cordon to avoid immediate evictions: `kube drain pool-2 --grace-period=120`
emi: (typo) eli: pool drain initiated, draining 4 nodes. Estimated 6 minutes.
product-ops: filing customer comms draft: "We experienced elevated latencies and timeouts for hosted API customers between 01:20-01:35 UTC due to a high-context warmup regression in a canary model rollout. We paused the rollout and routed traffic to a stable model version. Working on permanent fix."
oncall-night: any way to reduce memory footprint quickly without rolling back model binary? e.g., enforce max_context override at router?
mike: yes, we can inject runtime param: `max_context=2048` for v13 via feature flag gateway; will clip very long sessions and reduce KV pressure. But it changes behavior. Recommend as short-term toggle for non-Dedicated traffic.
sarah: opted in for hosted traffic only, flipping feature flag now. `gatewayctl set-flag v13.max_context 2048 --scope=hosted` -> done.
oncall-night: metrics now — queue length dropping, GPU mem freed as evictions finish, p95 down to ~420ms, error rate down to 0.4%. Good.
eli: quota request opened with cloud-ops: ticket #CO-54321 requesting bump from 5 -> 8 pools, ETA unknown but flagged urgent.
oncall-night: still need permanent fix: root cause likely v13 increasing per-session KV-cache due to context normalization logic; add postmortem item to require model onboarding eval with simulated context distribution. Assign owner?
sarah: assigning to eli for infra follow-up and mike for model/regression.
oncall-night: customer impact summary for now: ~15 minutes impact window, ~2.8% peak 500s for hosted generation endpoints, ~3 customers reported. Escalation to SEs queued.
cs-rep: pushing the comms to impacted customers now.
oncall-night: handing off to night->day oncall at 02:15 UTC. Handoff notes: paused canary, routing fallback active, eviction complete, pool drain to free quota in progress, quota request submitted. Postmortem owners: eli (infra quota & autoscaler), mike (model KV regression), sarah (deploy safety/playbook). Handoff ack: @matt-day oncall please pick up.
matt-day: ack, taking over. Summary received. I'll keep the ticket open and watch for quota closure.
oncall-night: closing P1 pager for now — mitigation stable but incident remains in monitoring. Please add timeline entries to the incident doc: https://incidents.example/2340156789
eli: note: logs show v13 warmup created many large KV entries due to new tokenization change; fix: cap kv entry size in runtime and add warmup backoff.
mike: also adding an eval to CI that runs the v13 model against long context synthetic load to catch this.
sarah: final note: we'll schedule a controlled canary reattempt only after fixes and a dark-canary run.
product-ops: creating postmortem with impact and action items. ETA for draft EOD.
cs-rep: customers informed. No additional major escalations.
